{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MbNq69AAF8kmYmZkwNXWR5","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Genensys LLC — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: http://www.genensys.com/\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Genensys LLC is a small, privately held healthcare IT company based in Oviedo, Florida (Orlando metro area). The company has approximately 11–12 employees and an estimated annual revenue of ~$7 million. Genensys develops EMR/EHR and practice management software primarily targeting small to mid-sized independent and specialty practices, with a notable focus on pediatric therapy clinics (speech therapy, occupational therapy, physical therapy, applied behavior therapy). The company also offers revenue cycle management services, digital marketing for medical practices, and HIPAA compliance consulting. The company appears to be founder-led (Farhan Shamsi is listed as the primary contact).\n     9→\n    10→Genensys operates a product ecosystem under the \"Simplify\" brand, including Simplify EMR (the general-purpose certified EHR), Simplify Therapy (a therapy-focused variant/configuration), and Simplify SMP (a School Medicaid Program billing tool for school districts). The company positions itself on affordability, ease of use, and customizability relative to larger EHR vendors.\n    11→\n    12→## Product: Simplify EMR\n    13→\n    14→CHPL IDs: 10317 (15.05.05.1523.GENS.01.00.1.200225)\n    15→\n    16→### What It Is\n    17→\n    18→Simplify EMR v4.0 is a cloud-based, ONC-certified EHR and integrated practice management system designed for ambulatory clinics of all sizes. The certification is broad — 35+ criteria spanning clinical documentation (a)(1)–(a)(14), transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(2), patient portal (e)(1)–(e)(2), public health reporting (f)(1)–(f)(2), FHIR APIs (g)(7)–(g)(10), and direct messaging (h)(1). The system was certified in February 2020 and remains active.\n    19→\n    20→The certified product appears to encompass the full Simplify EMR platform, which includes the EHR, practice management, and patient portal as a unified system. The vendor describes it as \"fully unified\" — the EHR, scheduling, billing, and patient portal are integrated rather than separate bolt-on modules.\n    21→\n    22→The mandatory disclosures page notes that MDToolBox is required as additional software (likely for e-prescribing/EPCS functionality), and the system is web-based, requiring only a current web browser.\n    23→\n    24→### Users & Market\n    25→\n    26→**Target users:** Clinicians (physicians, therapists), nurses, billing staff, and practice managers at small to mid-sized independent practices. The FindEMR listing describes the target as \"practices with approximately six physicians or fewer.\"\n    27→\n    28→**Specialty focus:** The vendor has a strong emphasis on pediatric therapy practices (OT, PT, speech therapy, ABA), but also markets to general ambulatory clinics. The \"Simplify Therapy\" branding on their website targets pediatric therapy clinics specifically, while \"Simplify EMR\" is the general-purpose offering. Both appear to share the same underlying platform with specialty-specific configurations/templates.\n    29→\n    30→**Customer base:** No specific customer count is disclosed on the website. The company's small size (11–12 employees, ~$7M revenue) suggests a relatively small installed base, likely in the hundreds of practices or fewer. Testimonials on the site come from small practice owners who emphasize affordability.\n    31→\n    32→**Geography:** Primarily US-based; the company is in Florida and markets nationally.\n    33→\n    34→**Additional product — Simplify SMP:** Genensys also offers a School Medicaid Program billing tool that helps school districts manage Medicaid reimbursement for IDEA-related therapeutic services (speech, PT, OT, behavioral services, nursing, transportation). This integrates with the broader Simplify EMR ecosystem and manages billing/claims data for school-based therapy services.\n    35→\n    36→### Modules & Functionality\n    37→\n    38→Based on vendor website pages, mandatory disclosures, and third-party descriptions:\n    39→\n    40→**Electronic Health Records / Clinical Documentation:**\n    41→- Patient charting and clinical documentation with customizable templates\n    42→- Comprehensive patient records accessible in a consolidated view (\"one click on a patient's name will give you the entire record\")\n    43→- Designed to be \"fully customizable\" to individual practice workflows\n    44→- Supports CPOE for medications and laboratory orders (certified (a)(1))\n    45→- Drug-drug, drug-allergy, and drug-diagnosis interaction checking\n    46→- Demographics recording, problem list, medication list/reconciliation, medication allergy list (certified (a)(5)–(a)(8))\n    47→- Clinical decision support (certified (a)(6))\n    48→- Implantable device list (certified (a)(14))\n    49→- Family health history (certified (a)(12))\n    50→- Patient-specific education resources (certified (a)(13))\n    51→- Clinical quality measures reporting — tested with CQMs including depression screening, specialist referral follow-up, medication documentation, BMI screening, high-risk medication use in elderly, blood pressure control\n    52→\n    53→**E-Prescribing (EPCS):**\n    54→- Electronic prescribing including controlled substances\n    55→- Integrated with MDToolBox (required additional software per disclosures)\n    56→- Connections to \"over 40,000 pharmacies across the country\"\n    57→- Medication history, prescription benefits, formulary data\n    58→- Age and weight-based dosing adjustments\n    59→- Treatment recommendations and dosage guidance\n    60→\n    61→**Laboratory Integration:**\n    62→- Electronic lab ordering and result receipt\n    63→- Lab result trending and comparison (current vs. past results)\n    64→- Alerts for abnormal results\n    65→- Task assignment for lab follow-up\n    66→- Advanced lab reporting\n    67→\n    68→**Practice Management / Scheduling:**\n    69→- Enterprise scheduling integrated with patient records\n    70→- Automated messaging services and appointment reminders\n    71→- Billing and claims management\n    72→- Rules-based claims editing (vendor claims 40% error reduction)\n    73→- Eligibility checks\n    74→- Responsibility estimator for point-of-service collections\n    75→- Authorization management\n    76→- Revenue cycle management (billing, credentialing, denial management, AR management)\n    77→\n    78→**Patient Portal:**\n    79→- Secure online access to medical records and clinical summaries\n    80→- Online bill pay (credit card)\n    81→- Patient-provider messaging\n    82→- Appointment request submission\n    83→- Prescription renewal requests\n    84→- Lab results viewing\n    85→- Educational materials access\n    86→- Email reminders for upcoming appointments\n    87→\n    88→**Interoperability / Data Exchange:**\n    89→- FHIR APIs for third-party access (certified (g)(7), (g)(9), (g)(10))\n    90→- Direct messaging (certified (h)(1))\n    91→- Transitions of care / C-CDA exchange (certified (b)(1), (b)(2))\n    92→- Connections to health information exchanges, pharmacies, payers, imaging services, hospital networks, referring providers, immunization registries, and specialty registries\n    93→- Public health reporting: immunization registry (f)(1) and syndromic surveillance (f)(2)\n    94→\n    95→**Telehealth:**\n    96→- Tele-therapy / telemedicine services mentioned on the website, though details are sparse\n    97→\n    98→**Reporting & Analytics:**\n    99→- Data mining reports\n   100→- Intelligent billing reports\n   101→- Pediatric-specific dashboard monitoring (for therapy variant)\n   102→\n   103→### Data & Content\n   104→\n   105→Based on the features described above, Simplify EMR stores and manages:\n   106→\n   107→- **Patient demographics** — standard demographic data\n   108→- **Clinical records** — problem lists, medication lists, allergy lists, medication history, family health history, implantable device lists, clinical notes/charting\n   109→- **Orders** — medication orders (CPOE), lab orders\n   110→- **Prescriptions** — e-prescribing data including controlled substances, medication history, formulary data, prescription benefits\n   111→- **Lab results** — electronic lab results with trending data and historical comparisons\n   112→- **Clinical quality measures** — CQM data for reporting (depression screening, BMI, blood pressure, etc.)\n   113→- **Scheduling data** — appointments, reminders, automated messages\n   114→- **Billing/claims data** — claims, eligibility records, authorization data, payment data, AR data\n   115→- **Patient portal data** — messages, prescription renewal requests, appointment requests, bill payments\n   116→- **Care coordination** — C-CDA documents, transition of care records, direct messages\n   117→- **Public health data** — immunization registry submissions, syndromic surveillance data\n   118→- **Audit logs** — required by (d) criteria certifications\n   119→- **User/provider data** — multi-factor authentication, access controls, user profiles\n   120→\n   121→The mandatory disclosures state there are \"no additional costs for the certified functionality\" — all features are included in the base subscription, with recurring fees for support and licensing.\n   122→\n   123→**Information gaps:** The vendor website provides limited detail on specific data fields or database structure. There is no public documentation of the data model. The therapy-specific features (pediatric dashboards, therapy-specific templates) suggest additional specialty data structures, but these are not detailed on the website.\n   124→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. The company has approximately 11–12 employees and an estimated annual revenue of ~$7 million. Genensys develops EMR/EHR and practice management software primarily targeting small to mid-sized independent and specialty practices, with a notable focus on pediatric therapy clinics (speech therapy, occupational therapy, physical therapy, applied behavior therapy). The company also offers revenue cycle management services, digital marketing for medical practices, and HIPAA compliance consulting. The company appears to be founder-led (Farhan Shamsi is listed as the primary contact).\n\nGenensys operates a product ecosystem under the \"Simplify\" brand, including Simplify EMR (the general-purpose certified EHR), Simplify Therapy (a therapy-focused variant/configuration), and Simplify SMP (a School Medicaid Program billing tool for school districts). The company positions itself on affordability, ease of use, and customizability relative to larger EHR vendors.\n\n## Product: Simplify EMR\n\nCHPL IDs: 10317 (15.05.05.1523.GENS.01.00.1.200225)\n\n### What It Is\n\nSimplify EMR v4.0 is a cloud-based, ONC-certified EHR and integrated practice management system designed for ambulatory clinics of all sizes. The certification is broad — 35+ criteria spanning clinical documentation (a)(1)–(a)(14), transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(2), patient portal (e)(1)–(e)(2), public health reporting (f)(1)–(f)(2), FHIR APIs (g)(7)–(g)(10), and direct messaging (h)(1). The system was certified in February 2020 and remains active.\n\nThe certified product appears to encompass the full Simplify EMR platform, which includes the EHR, practice management, and patient portal as a unified system. The vendor describes it as \"fully unified\" — the EHR, scheduling, billing, and patient portal are integrated rather than separate bolt-on modules.\n\nThe mandatory disclosures page notes that MDToolBox is required as additional software (likely for e-prescribing/EPCS functionality), and the system is web-based, requiring only a current web browser.\n\n### Users & Market\n\n**Target users:** Clinicians (physicians, therapists), nurses, billing staff, and practice managers at small to mid-sized independent practices. The FindEMR listing describes the target as \"practices with approximately six physicians or fewer.\"\n\n**Specialty focus:** The vendor has a strong emphasis on pediatric therapy practices (OT, PT, speech therapy, ABA), but also markets to general ambulatory clinics. The \"Simplify Therapy\" branding on their website targets pediatric therapy clinics specifically, while \"Simplify EMR\" is the general-purpose offering. Both appear to share the same underlying platform with specialty-specific configurations/templates.\n\n**Customer base:** No specific customer count is disclosed on the website. The company's small size (11–12 employees, ~$7M revenue) suggests a relatively small installed base, likely in the hundreds of practices or fewer. Testimonials on the site come from small practice owners who emphasize affordability.\n\n**Geography:** Primarily US-based; the company is in Florida and markets nationally.\n\n**Additional product — Simplify SMP:** Genensys also offers a School Medicaid Program billing tool that helps school districts manage Medicaid reimbursement for IDEA-related therapeutic services (speech, PT, OT, behavioral services, nursing, transportation). This integrates with the broader Simplify EMR ecosystem and manages billing/claims data for school-based therapy services.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor website pages, mandatory disclosures, and third-party descriptions:\n\n**Electronic Health Records / Clinical Documentation:**\n- Patient charting and clinical documentation with customizable templates\n- Comprehensive patient records accessible in a consolidated view (\"one click on a patient's name will give you the entire record\")\n- Designed to be \"fully customizable\" to individual practice workflows\n- Supports CPOE for medications and laboratory orders (certified (a)(1))\n- Drug-drug, drug-allergy, and drug-diagnosis interaction checking\n- Demographics recording, problem list, medication list/reconciliation, medication allergy list (certified (a)(5)–(a)(8))\n- Clinical decision support (certified (a)(6))\n- Implantable device list (certified (a)(14))\n- Family health history (certified (a)(12))\n- Patient-specific education resources (certified (a)(13))\n- Clinical quality measures reporting — tested with CQMs including depression screening, specialist referral follow-up, medication documentation, BMI screening, high-risk medication use in elderly, blood pressure control\n\n**E-Prescribing (EPCS):**\n- Electronic prescribing including controlled substances\n- Integrated with MDToolBox (required additional software per disclosures)\n- Connections to \"over 40,000 pharmacies across the country\"\n- Medication history, prescription benefits, formulary data\n- Age and weight-based dosing adjustments\n- Treatment recommendations and dosage guidance\n\n**Laboratory Integration:**\n- Electronic lab ordering and result receipt\n- Lab result trending and comparison (current vs. past results)\n- Alerts for abnormal results\n- Task assignment for lab follow-up\n- Advanced lab reporting\n\n**Practice Management / Scheduling:**\n- Enterprise scheduling integrated with patient records\n- Automated messaging services and appointment reminders\n- Billing and claims management\n- Rules-based claims editing (vendor claims 40% error reduction)\n- Eligibility checks\n- Responsibility estimator for point-of-service collections\n- Authorization management\n- Revenue cycle management (billing, credentialing, denial management, AR management)\n\n**Patient Portal:**\n- Secure online access to medical records and clinical summaries\n- Online bill pay (credit card)\n- Patient-provider messaging\n- Appointment request submission\n- Prescription renewal requests\n- Lab results viewing\n- Educational materials access\n- Email reminders for upcoming appointments\n\n**Interoperability / Data Exchange:**\n- FHIR APIs for third-party access (certified (g)(7), (g)(9), (g)(10))\n- Direct messaging (certified (h)(1))\n- Transitions of care / C-CDA exchange (certified (b)(1), (b)(2))\n- Connections to health information exchanges, pharmacies, payers, imaging services, hospital networks, referring providers, immunization registries, and specialty registries\n- Public health reporting: immunization registry (f)(1) and syndromic surveillance (f)(2)\n\n**Telehealth:**\n- Tele-therapy / telemedicine services mentioned on the website, though details are sparse\n\n**Reporting & Analytics:**\n- Data mining reports\n- Intelligent billing reports\n- Pediatric-specific dashboard monitoring (for therapy variant)\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the features described above, Simplify EMR stores and manages:\n\n- **Patient demographics** — standard demographic data\n- **Clinical records** — problem lists, medication lists, allergy lists, medication history, family health history, implantable device lists, clinical notes/charting\n- **Orders** — medication orders (CPOE), lab orders\n- **Prescriptions** — e-prescribing data including controlled substances, medication history, formulary data, prescription benefits\n- **Lab results** — electronic lab results with trending data and historical comparisons\n- **Clinical quality measures** — CQM data for reporting (depression screening, BMI, blood pressure, etc.)\n- **Scheduling data** — appointments, reminders, automated messages\n- **Billing/claims data** — claims, eligibility records, authorization data, payment data, AR data\n- **Patient portal data** — messages, prescription renewal requests, appointment requests, bill payments\n- **Care coordination** — C-CDA documents, transition of care records, direct messages\n- **Public health data** — immunization registry submissions, syndromic surveillance data\n- **Audit logs** — required by (d) criteria certifications\n- **User/provider data** — multi-factor authentication, access controls, user profiles\n\nThe mandatory disclosures state there are \"no additional costs for the certified functionality\" — all features are included in the base subscription, with recurring fees for support and licensing.\n\n**Information gaps:** The vendor website provides limited detail on specific data fields or database structure. There is no public documentation of the data model. The therapy-specific features (pediatric dashboards, therapy-specific templates) suggest additional specialty data structures, but these are not detailed on the website.\n","numLines":124,"startLine":1,"totalLines":124}}}

All fees associated with the additional software required are included in our monthly recurring support fees. This solution is web based, requires the use of a current web browser and may require the execution of a contract and business associates agreement. API Information: SimplifyEMR v4.0 has created a set of APIs (Application Programming Interface) to provide third-party software developers with access to health information. Services. This certification does not represent an endorsement by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. Vendor Genensys LLC Product Version SimplifyEMR v4.0 Criteria Certified see Modules Tested and Certified table below Version 4.0 Certification # 15.05.05.1523.GENS.01.00.1.200225 ONC Certification / Date Feb 25, 2020     Additional Software Required MDToolBox Simplify EMR V4.0 is certified for the following Modules     Tested and Certified Clinical Quality Measures CMS2v8 Preventive Care and Screening: Screening for Depression and Follow-Up Plan CMS50v7 Closing the Referral Loop: Receipt of Specialist Report CMS68v8 Documentation of Current Medications in the Medical Record CMS69v7 Preventive Care and Screening: Body Mass Index (BMI) Screening and Follow-Up Plan CMS156v7 Use of High-Risk Medications in the Elderly CMS165v7 Controlling High Blood Pressure Modules Tested and Certified 315 (a) (1) Computerized Provider Order Entry (CPOE) – Medications (2) Computerized provider order entry (CPOE) – laboratory (4) Drug-Drug, Drug-Allergy Interaction Checks for CPOE (5)  Demographics (12) Family Health History (14) Implantable Device List 315 (b) (1) Transitions of Care (2) Clinical Information Reconciliation and Incorporation (10) Electronic Health Information Export (11) decision support interventions 315 (c) (1) Clinical Quality Measures – Record and Export 315 (d) (1) Authentication, Access Control, Authorization (2) Auditable Events and Tamper-Resistance (3) Audit Report(s) (4) Amendments (5) Automatic Access Time-out (6) Emergency Access (7) End-User Device Encryption (8) Integrity (9) Trusted Connection (10) Auditing Actions on Health Information (12 ) Encrypt authentication credentials (13) Multi-factor authentication 315 (e) (1) View, Download, and Transmit to 3rd Party 315 (f) (1) Transmission to Immunization Registries (2) Transmission to public health agencies — syndromic surveillance 315 (g) (3) Safety-Enhanced Design (4) Quality Management System (5) Accessibility-Centered Design (6) Consolidated CDA Creation (7) Application Access – Patient Selection (10)  Standardized API for patient and population services (9) Application Access – All Data Request 315 (h) (1) Direct Project Costs : As part of the client service agreement, this certified product may have recurring and /or one-time fees for support and licensing. There are no additional costs for the certified functionality; the features are incorporated into the product at no additional costs to clients. All fees associated with the additional software required are included in our monthly recurring support fees. This solution is web based, requires the use of a current web browser and may require the execution of a contract and business associates agreement. API Information: SimplifyEMR v4.0 has created a set of APIs (Application Programming Interface) to provide third-party software developers with access to health information. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_019j1tPXhyrdEAnm98xCxZrU","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01XAvgrRwWBbzj8dKNK6MiWL","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/genensys-llc--simplify-emr/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Genensys LLC — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HsYw7-fWQW-6txwQBw0OcsT0M5H7Wxnv7A2YopWGXSo/edit?usp=sharing\n- CHPL IDs: 10317 (15.05.05.1523.GENS.01.00.1.200225)\n- Product: Simplify EMR v4.0\n- Certification date: 2020-02-25\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. Probed the registered URL with `curl -sI -L`. It's a Google Docs document returning HTTP 200 with `text/html; charset=utf-8`.\n\n2. Exported the document in three formats using Google's export API:\n   ```\n   curl -sL \"https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HsYw7-fWQW-6txwQBw0OcsT0M5H7Wxnv7A2YopWGXSo/export?format=pdf\" -o ehi-export-doc.pdf\n   curl -sL \"https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HsYw7-fWQW-6txwQBw0OcsT0M5H7Wxnv7A2YopWGXSo/export?format=txt\" -o ehi-export-doc.txt\n   curl -sL \"https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HsYw7-fWQW-6txwQBw0OcsT0M5H7Wxnv7A2YopWGXSo/export?format=docx\" -o ehi-export-doc.docx\n   ```\n\n3. Verified the PDF: `pdfinfo` confirms 2 pages, title \"Simplify EMR b(10) Export Format\", produced by Google Docs Renderer.\n\n4. Opened the document in Chrome and took screenshots of both pages. The document has a title page (\"Simplify EMR / Export Format\") and a single content page with the export format description.\n\n5. Checked the mandatory disclosures page at `https://genensys.com/mu-disclosure/` — it confirms (b)(10) certification but contains no additional EHI export documentation or download links.\n\n6. Checked the vendor's API documentation page at `https://genensys.com/api/` — it contains links to g(10) FHIR API documentation, API terms, and an API framework page. These are all related to the (g)(10) standardized API, not the (b)(10) export. The b(10) export described in the Google Doc is a separate C-CDA + documents export mechanism, not FHIR-based.\n\n7. No additional EHI export documentation was found anywhere on the vendor's site.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a single Google Doc (831 bytes of text, 2 PDF pages) titled \"Simplify EMR b(10) Export Format.\" The document describes two export modes:\n\n### All Patient Mode\n- Produces a ZIP file named `Patient_export_{date}.zip`\n- Contains one folder per patient, each in the single-patient format described below\n\n### Single Patient Mode\n- Creates a folder named `Lastname_FirstName_patientId_Date`\n- The folder contains:\n  1. **A C-CDA file** (`Lastname_FirstName_ccda.xml`) — described as \"Conformant to USCDI v1\" with a reference to the USCDI Version 1 July 2020 Errata document for C-CDA specifications\n  2. **Encounters subfolder** — contains all visit notes as PDF or HTML files, named `{encounterId}_{date}.pdf` or `.html` (0 to many)\n  3. **Patient Documents subfolder** — contains other documents as PDF or HTML files, named `{documentId}_{date}.pdf` or `.html` (0 to many)\n\nThat is the entirety of the documentation. There is no data dictionary, no field-level documentation, no schema file, no sample data, no export instructions, and no description of what data fields are included in the C-CDA or what types of documents appear in the subfolders.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThe export format relies on two mechanisms to cover EHI:\n1. A **USCDI v1 C-CDA document** per patient\n2. **Encounter notes and patient documents** as PDF/HTML files\n\n**What USCDI v1 C-CDA covers** (standardized clinical summary data):\n- Demographics, problems, medications, allergies, immunizations, vital signs, lab results, procedures, care team, goals, health concerns, assessment/plan, clinical notes (some), implantable devices\n\n**What appears to be missing or undocumented** from the product's known data stores:\n- **Billing/claims data** — The product has integrated practice management with billing, claims, eligibility, authorization, and revenue cycle management. None of this is mentioned in the export documentation. C-CDA does not carry billing data. No separate billing export is described.\n- **Scheduling data** — Appointments, reminders, automated messages are part of the PM system but not covered by C-CDA or the export.\n- **E-prescribing data** — While medication lists appear in C-CDA, the full e-prescribing transaction history (via MDToolBox integration), prescription benefits, formulary data, and controlled substance prescribing records are unlikely to be fully captured.\n- **Patient portal data** — Messages between patients and providers, prescription renewal requests, appointment requests, bill payment records — none of these are mentioned or covered by C-CDA.\n- **Lab ordering details** — C-CDA includes lab results but not the full ordering workflow, task assignments, or trending data the product stores.\n- **Clinical quality measure data** — CQM reporting data is part of the certified system but not addressed in the export.\n- **Therapy-specific data** — The product has a strong focus on pediatric therapy (OT, PT, speech, ABA) with specialty-specific templates, dashboards, and workflows. None of this specialty clinical data is specifically addressed. It may partially appear in encounter notes as PDFs, but there's no structured export of therapy-specific assessments.\n- **Custom form/template data** — The product emphasizes customizability with configurable templates. Structured data from custom forms may be lost when rendered as PDF encounter notes.\n\nThe encounter PDFs/HTMLs may capture some clinical narrative data beyond what's in C-CDA, but rendering clinical notes as PDF/HTML means the structured data (coded diagnoses, measurements, therapy progress metrics) becomes unstructured and non-computable.\n\n**Bottom line:** This export appears to be a thin wrapper around C-CDA (covering USCDI v1 clinical summaries) plus document dumps. It is essentially a (g)(6)-style clinical summary export repackaged as a (b)(10) export, with encounter notes added as flat documents. The export does not appear to cover \"all electronic health information\" — billing, scheduling, patient portal interactions, therapy-specific structured data, and e-prescribing workflow data are all absent.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Primary format:** USCDI v1 C-CDA XML (one per patient)\n- **Supplementary format:** PDF and/or HTML files for encounter notes and patient documents\n- **Packaging:** ZIP file (all-patient mode) or folder (single-patient mode)\n- **Standard compliance:** Claims conformance to USCDI v1 C-CDA. References the official USCDI Version 1 errata document.\n- **No proprietary schema or data dictionary** is provided.\n\nThe format choice is problematic for a (b)(10) export. C-CDA is designed for clinical summaries — it covers USCDI data classes well but cannot represent billing records, scheduling data, patient portal interactions, or arbitrary specialty-specific clinical structures. A true (b)(10) export of \"all EHI\" from a practice management system with billing would need a separate mechanism (CSV, database dump, etc.) for data that doesn't fit into C-CDA.\n\nA third party could reconstruct a clinical summary from this export but could **not** reconstruct the full patient record including billing history, e-prescribing transactions, portal messages, or specialty therapy assessments.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is **extremely minimal** — 831 bytes of plain text describing only the folder structure and file naming conventions. There is:\n\n- **No data dictionary** — no field/element definitions for the C-CDA content\n- **No value sets or coded field documentation**\n- **No sample data or example exports**\n- **No user guide or instructions** for performing the export\n- **No screenshots of the export interface**\n- **No description of what clinical data elements** are included in the C-CDA\n- **No description of what types of encounter notes or documents** appear in the subfolders\n- **No error handling or edge case documentation**\n- **No versioning or change history**\n\nThe only external reference is to the USCDI v1 errata document for C-CDA specifications, which is a standard reference — it tells you what C-CDA can contain but not what Simplify EMR actually puts into its C-CDA exports.\n\nA developer attempting to import this data would need to treat the C-CDA as a generic USCDI v1 document and the encounter/document files as opaque blobs. There is no vendor-specific documentation to guide the process.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity:** File/folder naming conventions only. No field-level documentation whatsoever.\n- **Coded fields:** Not documented.\n- **Relationships:** Not documented beyond the folder hierarchy (patient → C-CDA + encounters + documents).\n- **Completeness:** The documentation describes the container format (folders and files) but not the content. Knowing that a file is named `Lastname_FirstName_ccda.xml` tells you nothing about what clinical data it contains or how complete it is.\n\nThis is among the most minimal EHI export documentation possible — it describes how files are organized in folders but provides zero insight into the data content, coverage, or format details.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HsYw7-fWQW-6txwQBw0OcsT0M5H7Wxnv7A2YopWGXSo/edit?usp=sharing\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (Google Docs export API works with curl)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- No obstacles encountered. The Google Doc was publicly accessible and exportable via curl.\n- The vendor's API documentation page (https://genensys.com/api/) contains only (g)(10) FHIR API documentation, which is a separate system from the (b)(10) export.\n- The mandatory disclosures page (https://genensys.com/mu-disclosure/) confirms (b)(10) certification but provides no additional export documentation.\n- No additional EHI export documentation was found on the vendor's website.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":620,"cache_read_input_tokens":63659,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":620},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"af244a2e-8618-41fe-89bf-b6f9d9524c0d","uuid":"1d285b41-ac4f-4230-9382-2538cb3f106d"}

These are all related to the (g)(10) standardized API, not the (b)(10) export. The b(10) export described in the Google Doc is a separate C-CDA + documents export mechanism, not FHIR-based.\n\n7. No additional EHI export documentation was found anywhere on the vendor's site.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a single Google Doc (831 bytes of text, 2 PDF pages) titled \"Simplify EMR b(10) Export Format.\" The document describes two export modes:\n\n### All Patient Mode\n- Produces a ZIP file named `Patient_export_{date}.zip`\n- Contains one folder per patient, each in the single-patient format described below\n\n### Single Patient Mode\n- Creates a folder named `Lastname_FirstName_patientId_Date`\n- The folder contains:\n  1. **A C-CDA file** (`Lastname_FirstName_ccda.xml`) — described as \"Conformant to USCDI v1\" with a reference to the USCDI Version 1 July 2020 Errata document for C-CDA specifications\n  2. **Encounters subfolder** — contains all visit notes as PDF or HTML files, named `{encounterId}_{date}.pdf` or `.html` (0 to many)\n  3. **Patient Documents subfolder** — contains other documents as PDF or HTML files, named `{documentId}_{date}.pdf` or `.html` (0 to many)\n\nThat is the entirety of the documentation. There is no data dictionary, no field-level documentation, no schema file, no sample data, no export instructions, and no description of what data fields are included in the C-CDA or what types of documents appear in the subfolders.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThe export format relies on two mechanisms to cover EHI:\n1. A **USCDI v1 C-CDA document** per patient\n2. **Encounter notes and patient documents** as PDF/HTML files\n\n**What USCDI v1 C-CDA covers** (standardized clinical summary data):\n- Demographics, problems, medications, allergies, immunizations, vital signs, lab results, procedures, care team, goals, health concerns, assessment/plan, clinical notes (some), implantable devices\n\n**What appears to be missing or undocumented** from the product's known data stores:\n- **Billing/claims data** — The product has integrated practice management with billing, claims, eligibility, authorization, and revenue cycle management. None of this is mentioned in the export documentation. C-CDA does not carry billing data. No separate billing export is described.\n- **Scheduling data** — Appointments, reminders, automated messages are part of the PM system but not covered by C-CDA or the export.\n- **E-prescribing data** — While medication lists appear in C-CDA, the full e-prescribing transaction history (via MDToolBox integration), prescription benefits, formulary data, and controlled substance prescribing records are unlikely to be fully captured.\n- **Patient portal data** — Messages between patients and providers, prescription renewal requests, appointment requests, bill payment records — none of these are mentioned or covered by C-CDA.\n- **Lab ordering details** — C-CDA includes lab results but not the full ordering workflow, task assignments, or trending data the product stores.\n- **Clinical quality measure data** — CQM reporting data is part of the certified system but not addressed in the export.\n- **Therapy-specific data** — The product has a strong focus on pediatric therapy (OT, PT, speech, ABA) with specialty-specific templates, dashboards, and workflows. None of this specialty clinical data is specifically addressed. It may partially appear in encounter notes as PDFs, but there's no structured export of therapy-specific assessments.\n- **Custom form/template data** — The product emphasizes customizability with configurable templates. Structured data from custom forms may be lost when rendered as PDF encounter notes.\n\nThe encounter PDFs/HTMLs may capture some clinical narrative data beyond what's in C-CDA, but rendering clinical notes as PDF/HTML means the structured data (coded diagnoses, measurements, therapy progress metrics) becomes unstructured and non-computable.\n\n**Bottom line:** This export appears to be a thin wrapper around C-CDA (covering USCDI v1 clinical summaries) plus document dumps. It is essentially a (g)(6)-style clinical summary export repackaged as a (b)(10) export, with encounter notes added as flat documents. The export does not appear to cover \"all electronic health information\" — billing, scheduling, patient portal interactions, therapy-specific structured data, and e-prescribing workflow data are all absent.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Primary format:** USCDI v1 C-CDA XML (one per patient)\n- **Supplementary format:** PDF and/or HTML files for encounter notes and patient documents\n- **Packaging:** ZIP file (all-patient mode) or folder (single-patient mode)\n- **Standard compliance:** Claims conformance to USCDI v1 C-CDA. References the official USCDI Version 1 errata document.\n- **No proprietary schema or data dictionary** is provided.\n\nThe format choice is problematic for a (b)(10) export. C-CDA is designed for clinical summaries — it covers USCDI data classes well but cannot represent billing records, scheduling data, patient portal interactions, or arbitrary specialty-specific clinical structures. A true (b)(10) export of \"all EHI\" from a practice management system with billing would need a separate mechanism (CSV, database dump, etc.) for data that doesn't fit into C-CDA.\n\nA third party could reconstruct a clinical summary from this export but could **not** reconstruct the full patient record including billing history, e-prescribing transactions, portal messages, or specialty therapy assessments.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is **extremely minimal** — 831 bytes of plain text describing only the folder structure and file naming conventions. There is:\n\n- **No data dictionary** — no field/element definitions for the C-CDA content\n- **No value sets or coded field documentation**\n- **No sample data or example exports**\n- **No user guide or instructions** for performing the export\n- **No screenshots of the export interface**\n- **No description of what clinical data elements** are included in the C-CDA\n- **No description of what types of encounter notes or documents** appear in the subfolders\n- **No error handling or edge case documentation**\n- **No versioning or change history**\n\nThe only external reference is to the USCDI v1 errata document for C-CDA specifications, which is a standard reference — it tells you what C-CDA can contain but not what Simplify EMR actually puts into its C-CDA exports.\n\nA developer attempting to import this data would need to treat the C-CDA as a generic USCDI v1 document and the encounter/document files as opaque blobs. There is no vendor-specific documentation to guide the process.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity:** File/folder naming conventions only. No field-level documentation whatsoever.\n- **Coded fields:** Not documented.\n- **Relationships:** Not documented beyond the folder hierarchy (patient → C-CDA + encounters + documents).\n- **Completeness:** The documentation describes the container format (folders and files) but not the content. Knowing that a file is named `Lastname_FirstName_ccda.xml` tells you nothing about what clinical data it contains or how complete it is.\n\nThis is among the most minimal EHI export documentation possible — it describes how files are organized in folders but provides zero insight into the data content, coverage, or format details.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HsYw7-fWQW-6txwQBw0OcsT0M5H7Wxnv7A2YopWGXSo/edit?usp=sharing\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (Google Docs export API works with curl)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- No obstacles encountered. The Google Doc was publicly accessible and exportable via curl.\n- The vendor's API documentation page (https://genensys.com/api/) contains only (g)(10) FHIR API documentation, which is a separate system from the (b)(10) export.\n- The mandatory disclosures page (https://genensys.com/mu-disclosure/) confirms (b)(10) certification but provides no additional export documentation.\n- No additional EHI export documentation was found on the vendor's website.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}
